requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The Ice Class Regulations of 2021 apply to ships contracted for construction on or after 5 July 2021. The provisions in section 1.8 (Ice classes) and chapter 2 (Ice Class Draught) in the 2021 Ice Class Regulations apply to all ships irrespective of their year of build.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The Ice Class Regulations of 2021 apply to ships contracted for construction on or after 5 July 2021. The provisions in section 1.8 (Ice classes) and chapter 2 (Ice Class Draught) in the 2021 Ice Class Regulations apply to all ships irrespective of their year of build.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The Ice Class Regulations of 2017 apply to ships contracted for construction on or after 1 January 2019 but before 5 July 2021.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The Ice Class Regulations of 2017 apply to ships contracted for construction on or after 1 January 2019 but before 5 July 2021.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The Ice Class Regulations of 2010 (TRAFI/31298/03.04.01.00/2010) apply to ships contracted for construction on or after 1 January 2012 but before 1 January 2019.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The Ice Class Regulations of 2010 (TRAFI/31298/03.04.01.00/2010) apply to ships contracted for construction on or after 1 January 2012 but before 1 January 2019.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The Ice Class Regulations of 2008 (8.12.2008 No. 2530/30/2008), issued by the Finnish Maritime Administration, apply to ships contracted for construction on or after 1 January 2010 but before 1 January 2012.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The Ice Class Regulations of 2008 (8.12.2008 No. 2530/30/2008), issued by the Finnish Maritime Administration, apply to ships contracted for construction on or after 1 January 2010 but before 1 January 2012.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The Ice Class Regulations of 2002 (20.9.2002 No. 5/30/2002), issued by the Finnish Maritime Administration, as amended, apply to ships the keels of which have been laid or which have been at a similar stage of construction on or after 1 September 2003 but which have been contracted for construction before 1 January 2010.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The Ice Class Regulations of 2002 (20.9.2002 No. 5/30/2002), issued by the Finnish Maritime Administration, as amended, apply to ships the keels of which have been laid or which have been at a similar stage of construction on or after 1 September 2003 but which have been contracted for construction before 1 January 2010.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The Board of Navigation Rules for Assigning Ships Separate Ice-Due Classes, 1985, (2.9.1985 No. 2575/85/307), as amended, apply to ships the keels of which have been laid or which have been at a similar stage of construction on or after 1 November 1986 but before 1 September 2003. On the owner's request, the requirements of the 2008 Ice Class Regulations may, however, be applied to the engine output of such ships.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The Board of Navigation Rules for Assigning Ships Separate Ice-Due Classes, 1985, (2.9.1985 No. 2575/85/307), as amended, apply to ships the keels of which have been laid or which have been at a similar stage of construction on or after 1 November 1986 but before 1 September 2003. On the owner's request, the requirements of the 2008 Ice Class Regulations may, however, be applied to the engine output of such ships.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: However, ships of ice class IA Super or IA the keels of which have been laid or which have been at a similar stage of construction before 1 September 2003 shall comply with the requirements in section 3.2.2 or 3.2.4 of the Ice Class Regulations of 2017 not later than 1 January in the year when twenty years have elapsed since the year the ship was delivered.
requirements.normalized_requirement: However, ships of ice class IA Super or IA the keels of which have been laid or which have been at a similar stage of construction before 1 September 2003 shall comply with the requirements in section 3.2.2 or 3.2.4 of the Ice Class Regulations of 2017 not later than 1 January in the year when twenty years have elapsed since the year the ship was delivered.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: Under section 3 of the Act on the Ice Classes of Ships and Icebreaker Assistance (1121/2005), ships are assigned to ice classes as follows:
requirements.normalized_requirement: Under section 3 of the Act on the Ice Classes of Ships and Icebreaker Assistance (1121/2005), ships are assigned to ice classes IA Super, IA, IB, IC, II, or III.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The upper ice waterline (UIWL) shall be the envelope of the highest points of the waterlines at which the ship is intended to operate in ice. The line may be a broken line.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The upper ice waterline (UIWL) shall be the envelope of the highest points of the waterlines at which the ship is intended to operate in ice. The line may be a broken line.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The lower ice waterline (LIWL) shall be the envelope of the lowest points of the waterlines at which the ship is intended to operate in ice. The line may be a broken line.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The lower ice waterline (LIWL) shall be the envelope of the lowest points of the waterlines at which the ship is intended to operate in ice. The line may be a broken line.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The maximum and minimum ice class draughts at fore and aft perpendiculars shall be determined in accordance with the upper and lower ice waterlines and the draught of the ship at fore and aft perpendiculars, when ice conditions require the ship to be ice-strengthened, shall always be between the upper and lower ice waterlines.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The maximum and minimum ice class draughts at fore and aft perpendiculars shall be determined in accordance with the upper and lower ice waterlines and the draught of the ship at fore and aft perpendiculars, when ice conditions require the ship to be ice-strengthened, shall always be between the upper and lower ice waterlines.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: Restrictions on draughts when operating in ice shall be documented and kept on board readily available to the master. The maximum and minimum ice class draughts fore, amidships and aft shall be indicated in the class certificate. For ships built on or after 1 July 2007, if the summer load line in fresh water is anywhere located at a higher level than the UIWL, the ship's sides are to be provided with a warning triangle and with an ice class draught mark at the maximum permissible ice class draught amidships (see Annex III). Ships built before 1 July 2007 shall be provided with such a marking, if the UIWL is below the summer load line, not later than the first scheduled dry docking after 1 July 2007.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Restrictions on draughts when operating in ice shall be documented and kept on board readily available to the master. The maximum and minimum ice class draughts fore, amidships and aft shall be indicated in the class certificate. For ships built on or after 1 July 2007, if the summer load line in fresh water is anywhere located at a higher level than the UIWL, the ship's sides are to be provided with a warning triangle and with an ice class draught mark at the maximum permissible ice class draught amidships (see Annex III). Ships built before 1 July 2007 shall be provided with such a marking, if the UIWL is below the summer load line, not later than the first scheduled dry docking after 1 July 2007.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The draught and trim, limited by the UIWL, must not be exceeded when the ship is navigating in ice. The salinity of the sea water along the intended route shall be taken into account when loading the ship.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The draught and trim, limited by the UIWL, must not be exceeded when the ship is navigating in ice. The salinity of the sea water along the intended route shall be taken into account when loading the ship.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The ship shall always be loaded down at least to the draught of LIWL amidships when navigating in ice. Any ballast tank, situated above the LIWL and needed to load down the ship to this water line, shall be equipped with devices to prevent the water from freezing. In determining the LIWL, regard shall be paid to the need to ensure a reasonable degree of ice-going capability in ballast. The highest point of the propeller shall be submerged and if possible at a depth of at least h_i below the water surface in all loading conditions. The forward draught shall be at least (2 + 0.00025*Delta)*h_i [m], but need not exceed 4*h_i (2.1), where Delta is the displacement of the ship [t] determined from the waterline on the UIWL (see section 2.1). Where multiple waterlines are used for determining the UIWL, the displacement must be determined from the waterline corresponding to the greatest displacement. h_i is the level ice thickness [m] according to section 4.2.1.
requirements.normalized_requirement: When navigating in ice, draught_amidships_m >= LIWL_draught_amidships_m. Any ballast tank above LIWL that is needed to reach LIWL shall have freezing_prevention_present = true. propeller_highest_point_submerged = true. forward_draught_m >= min((2 + 0.00025*displacement_UIWL_t)*level_ice_thickness_m, 4*level_ice_thickness_m). If multiple UIWL waterlines exist, use the displacement at the greatest-displacement UIWL.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The engine output P is the total maximum output the propulsion machinery can continuously deliver to the propeller(s). If the output of the machinery is restricted by technical means or by any regulations applicable to the ship, P shall be taken as the restricted output. If additional power sources are available for propulsion power (e.g. shaft motors), in addition to the power of the main engine(s), they shall also be included in the total engine output.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The engine output P is the maximum output the propulsion machinery can continuously deliver to the propeller(s). If the output is restricted by technical means or regulations, P shall be taken as the restricted output.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The engine output shall not be less than that determined by the formula below and in no case less than 1,000 kW for ice class IA, IB and IC, and no less than 2,800 kW for IA Super.
requirements.normalized_requirement: IF iceClass IN {'IA','IB','IC'}, THEN mcrPower_kW >= max(calculated_required_power_kW, 1000). IF iceClass = 'IA Super', THEN mcrPower_kW >= max(calculated_required_power_kW, 2800).

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: To qualify for ice class IA Super, IA, IB or IC, a ship the keel of which is laid or which is at a similar stage of construction on or after 1 September 2003 shall comply with the following requirements regarding its engine output. The engine output requirement shall be calculated for two draughts by formula 3.1. Draughts to be used are the maximum draught amidships referred to as UIWL and the minimum draught amidships referred to as LIWL, as defined in section 2.2. In the calculations, the ship's parameters which depend on the draught must be determined at the appropriate draught, but L and B must be determined only at the UIWL. The engine output shall be no less than the greater of these two outputs. P_min = K_e*(R_CH/1000)^(3/2)/D_p [kW] (3.1), where K_e shall be given a value according to Table 3-1.
requirements.normalized_requirement: IF construction_stage_date >= '2003-09-01' AND iceClass IN {'IA Super','IA','IB','IC'}, THEN compute P_min = K_e*(R_CH/1000)^(3/2)/D_p at UIWL and LIWL; use draught-dependent inputs at the corresponding draught, use L and B at UIWL for both calculations, and require mcrPower_kW >= max(P_min_UIWL_kW, P_min_LIWL_kW). K_e shall be selected from Table 3-1.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: Coefficients f_1-f_4 and g_1-g_3 are given in Table 3-2. C_3 = 845 kg/(m^2*s^2), C_4 = 42 kg/(m^2*s^2), C_5 = 825 kg/s^2. psi = atan(tan(phi_2)/sin(alpha)). If the value of the term ((L*T)/B^2)^3 is less than 5, the value 5 shall be used; if the value is more than 20, the value 20 shall be used.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Set C_3 = 845 kg/(m^2*s^2), C_4 = 42 kg/(m^2*s^2), C_5 = 825 kg/s^2 and psi = atan(tan(phi_2)/sin(alpha)). Clamp ((L*T)/B^2)^3 to the inclusive interval [5, 20].

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: In order to retain ice class IB or IC a ship, to which ice class regulations 1985 (2.9.1985, No. 2575/85/307, as amended) apply, shall comply with the required minimum engine output as defined in section 3.2.1 of the ice class regulations 1985. For ease of reference, the provisions for ice classes IB and IC of section 3.2.1 of the ice class regulations 1985 are given in Annex II of these regulations.
requirements.normalized_requirement: In order to retain ice class IB or IC a ship, to which ice class regulations 1985 (2.9.1985, No. 2575/85/307, as amended) apply, shall comply with the required minimum engine output as defined in section 3.2.1 of the ice class regulations 1985. For ease of reference, the provisions for ice classes IB and IC of section 3.2.1 of the ice class regulations 1985 are given in Annex II of these regulations.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: In order to retain ice class IA Super or IA a ship, the keel of which has been laid or which has been at a similar stage of construction before 1 September 2003, shall comply with the requirements in section 3.2.2 above not later than 1 January in the year when twenty years have elapsed since the year the ship was delivered.
requirements.normalized_requirement: In order to retain ice class IA Super or IA a ship, the keel of which has been laid or which has been at a similar stage of construction before 1 September 2003, shall comply with the requirements in section 3.2.2 above not later than 1 January in the year when twenty years have elapsed since the year the ship was delivered.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: For ice class IA Super, ship without a bulb, C_1 and C_2 shall be calculated as follows: C_1 = f_1*(B*L)/(2*T/B + 1) + 1.84*(f_2*B + f_3*L + f_4*B*L). C_2 = 3.52*(g_1 + g_2*B) + g_3*(1 + 1.2*T/B)*B^2/sqrt(L).
requirements.normalized_requirement: For IA Super without a bulb, compute C_1=f_1*(B*L)/(2*T/B+1)+1.84*(f_2*B+f_3*L+f_4*B*L) and C_2=3.52*(g_1+g_2*B)+g_3*(1+1.2*T/B)*B^2/sqrt(L).

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: For ice class IA Super, ship with a bulb, C_1 and C_2 shall be calculated as follows: C_1 = f_1*(B*L)/(2*T/B + 1) + 2.89*(f_2*B + f_3*L + f_4*B*L). C_2 = 6.67*(g_1 + g_2*B) + g_3*(1 + 1.2*T/B)*B^2/sqrt(L).
requirements.normalized_requirement: For IA Super with a bulb, compute C_1=f_1*(B*L)/(2*T/B+1)+2.89*(f_2*B+f_3*L+f_4*B*L) and C_2=6.67*(g_1+g_2*B)+g_3*(1+1.2*T/B)*B^2/sqrt(L).

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: Coefficients f_1-f_4 and g_1-g_3 are given in Table 3-3. C_3 = 460 kg/(m^2*s^2), C_4 = 18.7 kg/(m^2*s^2), C_5 = 825 kg/s^2. If the value of the term ((L*T)/B^2)^3 is less than 5, the value 5 shall be used; if the value is more than 20, the value 20 shall be used.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Coefficients f_1-f_4 and g_1-g_3 are given in Table 3-3. C_3 = 460 kg/(m^2*s^2), C_4 = 18.7 kg/(m^2*s^2), C_5 = 825 kg/s^2. If the value of the term ((L*T)/B^2)^3 is less than 5, the value 5 shall be used; if the value is more than 20, the value 20 shall be used.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: Direct analyses are to be carried out using the load patch defined in section 4.2 (p, h and la). The pressure to be used is 1.8p where p is determined according to 4.2.2. The load patch must be applied at locations where the capacity of the structure under the combined effects of bending and shear is minimised. In particular, the structure must be checked with a load centred at the UIWL, 0.5h0 below the LIWL, and positioned at several vertical locations in between. Several horizontal locations shall also be checked, especially the locations centred at the mid-span or -spacing. Furthermore, if the load length la cannot be determined directly from the arrangement of the structure, several values of la shall be checked using corresponding values for ca.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Direct analyses are to be carried out using the load patch defined in section 4.2 (p, h and la). The pressure to be used is 1.8p where p is determined according to 4.2.2. The load patch must be applied at locations where the capacity of the structure under the combined effects of bending and shear is minimised. In particular, the structure must be checked with a load centred at the UIWL, 0.5h0 below the LIWL, and positioned at several vertical locations in between. Several horizontal locations shall also be checked, especially the locations centred at the mid-span or -spacing. Furthermore, if the load length la cannot be determined directly from the arrangement of the structure, several values of la shall be checked using corresponding values for ca.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The acceptance criterion for designs is that the combined stresses from bending and shear, when using the von Mises yield criterion, are lower than the yield point sigmay. When the direct calculation is based on beam theory, the allowable shear stress must be no larger than 0.9*tauy, where tauy = sigmay/sqrt3.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The acceptance criterion for designs is that the combined stresses from bending and shear, when using the von Mises yield criterion, are lower than the yield point sigmay. When the direct calculation is based on beam theory, the allowable shear stress must be no larger than 0.9*tauy, where tauy = sigmay/sqrt3.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: If scantlings derived from these regulations are less than those required by the classification society for a ship that has not been ice strengthened, the latter shall be used.
requirements.normalized_requirement: If scantlings derived from these regulations are less than those required by the classification society for a ship that has not been ice strengthened, the latter shall be used.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: NB3. The requirements for the section modulus and shear area of the frames, stringers and web frames in 4.4, 4.5 and 4.6 are in accordance with the effective member cross section. For cases where the member is not normal to the plating, the section properties must be calculated in accordance with the appropriate classification society rules for the ship in question.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: L shall be taken as the ship's rule length used by the classification society.
requirements.normalized_requirement: L shall be taken as the ship's rule length used by the classification society.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: An ice-strengthened ship is assumed to operate in open sea conditions corresponding to a level ice thickness not exceeding hi. The design ice load height (h) of the area actually under ice pressure at any particular point of time is, however, assumed to be only a fraction of the ice thickness. The values for hi and h are given in Table 4-1.
requirements.normalized_requirement: An ice-strengthened ship is assumed to operate in open sea conditions corresponding to a level ice thickness not exceeding hi. The design ice load height (h) of the area actually under ice pressure at any particular point of time is, however, assumed to be only a fraction of the ice thickness. The values for hi and h are given in Table 4-1.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The design ice pressure is determined by the formula p = c_d*c_p*c_a*p_0 [MPa] (4.1), where c_d is a factor which takes account of the influence of the size and engine output of the ship. The maximum value is c_d = 1. It is calculated using c_d = (a*k + b)/1000 (4.2).
requirements.normalized_requirement: The design ice pressure is determined by the formula p = c_d*c_p*c_a*p_0 [MPa] (4.1), where c_d is a factor which takes account of the influence of the size and engine output of the ship. The maximum value is c_d = 1. It is calculated using c_d = (a*k + b)/1000 (4.2).

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: For transverse framing, the thickness of the shell plating shall be determined by t = 667*s*sqrt(f_1*p_pl/sigma_y) + t_c [mm] (4.5). For longitudinal framing, the thickness shall be determined by t = 667*s*sqrt(p/(f_2*sigma_y)) + t_c [mm] (4.6).
requirements.normalized_requirement: For transverse framing, the thickness of the shell plating shall be determined by t = 667*s*sqrt(f_1*p_pl/sigma_y) + t_c [mm] (4.5). For longitudinal framing, the thickness shall be determined by t = 667*s*sqrt(p/(f_2*sigma_y)) + t_c [mm] (4.6).

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: f_2 = 0.4/(h/s) + 0.6 where h/s <= 1; f_2 = 1.4 - 0.4*(h/s) where 1 <= h/s <= 1.8. Here h is as given in section 4.2.1 and sigma_y is the yield stress of the material [N/mm^2]. Use sigma_y = 235 N/mm^2 for normal-strength hull structural steel and sigma_y = 315 N/mm^2 or higher for high-strength hull structural steel. If steels with different yield stress are used, actual accepted values may be substituted. The abrasion and corrosion increment t_c shall normally be 2 mm; a lower approved value may be used for a suitable maintained special surface coating.
requirements.normalized_requirement: f_2 = 0.4/(h/s) + 0.6 where h/s <= 1; f_2 = 1.4 - 0.4*(h/s) where 1 <= h/s <= 1.8. Here h is as given in section 4.2.1 and sigma_y is the yield stress of the material [N/mm^2]. Use sigma_y = 235 N/mm^2 for normal-strength hull structural steel and sigma_y = 315 N/mm^2 or higher for high-strength hull structural steel. If steels with different yield stress are used, actual accepted values may be substituted. The abrasion and corrosion increment t_c shall normally be 2 mm; a lower approved value may be used for a suitable maintained special surface coating.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The vertical extension of the ice strengthening of framing shall be at least as given in Table 4- 6. Where an upper bow ice belt is required (see 4.3.1), the ice-strengthened part of the framing shall be extended to at least the top of this ice belt. Where the ice-strengthening would go beyond a deck, the top or bottom plating of a tank or tank top by no more than 250 mm, it can be terminated at that deck, top or bottom plating of the tank or tank top.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Set the vertical extent of framing ice strengthening from Table 4-6. IF upper_bow_ice_belt_required = true, THEN framing_ice_strengthening_upper_extent >= upper_bow_ice_belt_top. IF extension_beyond_adjacent_deck_or_tank_boundary_mm <= 250, THEN termination_at_that_boundary is permitted.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The section modulus of a main or intermediate transverse frame shall be calculated using Z = p*s*h*l/(m_t*sigma_y)*10^6 [cm^3] (4.7), and the effective shear area shall be calculated using A = sqrt(3)*f_3*p*h*s/(2*sigma_y)*10^4 [cm^2] (4.8), where p is the ice pressure from 4.2.2, s is the frame spacing, h is the load-area height from 4.2.1, l is the frame span, m_t = 7*m_0/(7 - 5*h/l), f_3 = 1.2, sigma_y is the yield stress from 4.3.2, and m_0 is selected from Table 4-7 for the applicable boundary condition.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Compute m_t = 7*m_0/(7 - 5*h/l), Z_cm3 = p_MPa*s_m*h_m*l_m/(m_t*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^6, and A_cm2 = sqrt(3)*1.2*p_MPa*h_m*s_m/(2*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^4. Select m_0 from Table 4-7 for the frame boundary condition.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: Where less than 15% of the span, l, of the frame is situated within the ice-strengthening zone for frames as defined in 4.4.1, ordinary frame scantlings may be used.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Where less than 15% of the span, l, of the frame is situated within the ice-strengthening zone for frames as defined in 4.4.1, ordinary frame scantlings may be used.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The upper end of the strengthened part of a main frame and of an intermediate ice frame shall be attached to a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank or an ice stringer (section 4.5). Where a frame terminates above a deck or a stringer which is situated at or above the upper limit of the ice belt (section 4.3.1), the part above the deck or stringer may have the scantlings required by the classification society for an non ice-strengthened ship and the upper end of an intermediate frame may be connected to the adjacent frames by a horizontal member with the same scantlings as the main frame.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The upper end of the strengthened part of a main frame and of an intermediate ice frame shall be attached to a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank or an ice stringer (section 4.5). Where a frame terminates above a deck or a stringer which is situated at or above the upper limit of the ice belt (section 4.3.1), the part above the deck or stringer may have the scantlings required by the classification society for an non ice-strengthened ship and the upper end of an intermediate frame may be connected to the adjacent frames by a horizontal member with the same scantlings as the main frame.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The lower end of the strengthened part of a main frame and of an intermediate ice frame shall be attached to a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank, tank top or an ice stringer (section 4.5). Where an intermediate frame terminates below a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank, tank top or ice stringer which is situated at or below the lower limit of the ice belt (section 4.3.1), the lower end may be connected to the adjacent main frames by a horizontal member of the same scantlings as the main frames. Note that the main frames below the lower edge of the ice belt must be ice strengthened, see 4.4.1.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The lower end of the strengthened part of a main frame and of an intermediate ice frame shall be attached to a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank, tank top or an ice stringer (section 4.5). Where an intermediate frame terminates below a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank, tank top or ice stringer which is situated at or below the lower limit of the ice belt (section 4.3.1), the lower end may be connected to the adjacent main frames by a horizontal member of the same scantlings as the main frames. Note that the main frames below the lower edge of the ice belt must be ice strengthened, see 4.4.1.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The section modulus of a longitudinal frame shall be calculated using Z = f_4*p*h*l^2/(4*m*sigma_y)*10^6 [cm^3] (4.9). The effective shear area shall be A = sqrt(3)*f_4*f_5*p*h*l/(2*sigma_y)*10^4 [cm^2] (4.10). The bracket shear area shall not be included in the actual frame shear area. Use f_4 = 1 - 0.2*h/s, f_5 = 2.16, p from 4.2.2, h from 4.2.1, s as frame spacing, l as total frame span, m = 13.3 for a continuous beam with brackets unless a smaller factor is required by significantly different boundary conditions, and sigma_y from 4.3.2.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Compute f_4 = 1 - 0.2*h/s, Z_cm3 = f_4*p_MPa*h_m*l_m^2/(4*m*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^6, and A_cm2 = sqrt(3)*f_4*2.16*p_MPa*h_m*l_m/(2*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^4. Use m = 13.3 for a continuous beam with brackets unless the actual end field requires a smaller factor. Exclude bracket area from actual_frame_shear_area.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: Within the ice-strengthened area, all frames shall be effectively attached to all of the supporting structures. A longitudinal frame shall be attached by brackets to all supporting web frames and bulkheads. When a transversal frame terminates at a stringer or deck, a bracket or similar construction must be fitted. When a frame is running through the supporting structure, both sides of the web plate of the frame must be connected to the structure (by direct welding, collar plate or lug). When a bracket is installed, it must have at least the same thickness as the web plate of the frame and the edge must be appropriately stiffened against buckling.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Within the ice-strengthened area, all frames shall be effectively attached to all of the supporting structures. A longitudinal frame shall be attached by brackets to all supporting web frames and bulkheads. When a transversal frame terminates at a stringer or deck, a bracket or similar construction must be fitted. When a frame is running through the supporting structure, both sides of the web plate of the frame must be connected to the structure (by direct welding, collar plate or lug). When a bracket is installed, it must have at least the same thickness as the web plate of the frame and the edge must be appropriately stiffened against buckling.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The frames shall be attached to the shell by a double continuous weld. No scalloping is allowed (except when crossing shell plate butts).
requirements.normalized_requirement: The frames shall be attached to the shell by a double continuous weld. No scalloping is allowed (except when crossing shell plate butts).

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The web thickness of the frames shall be at least the maximum of: h_w*sqrt(sigma_y)/C, where C = 805 for profiles and C = 282 for flat bars; half of the net shell-plating thickness t - t_c; and 9 mm. Where a deck, tank top, tank bottom or bulkhead is used in lieu of a frame, its plate thickness shall be calculated in the same way using the adjacent frame height h_w and C = 805.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The web thickness of the frames shall be at least the maximum of: h_w*sqrt(sigma_y)/C, where C = 805 for profiles and C = 282 for flat bars; half of the net shell-plating thickness t - t_c; and 9 mm. Where a deck, tank top, tank bottom or bulkhead is used in lieu of a frame, its plate thickness shall be calculated in the same way using the adjacent frame height h_w and C = 805.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: Asymmetrical frames and frames which are not at right angles to the shell (web less than 90 degrees to the shell) shall be supported against tripping by brackets, intercoastals, stringers or similar, at a distance not exceeding 1,300 mm. For frames with spans greater than 4 m, the extent of antitripping supports must be applied to all regions and for all ice classes. For frames with spans less than or equal to 4 m, the extent of antitripping supports must be applied to all regions for ice class IA Super, to the bow and midbody regions for ice class IA, and to the bow region for ice classes IB and IC. Direct calculation methods may be applied to demonstrate the equivalent level of support provided by alternative arrangements.
requirements.normalized_requirement: IF frame_asymmetrical = true OR frame_web_angle_to_shell_deg < 90, THEN antitripping_support_spacing_mm <= 1300. IF frame_span_m > 4, THEN antitripping_support_scope = 'all regions/all ice classes'. IF frame_span_m <= 4, THEN required scope is all regions for IA Super, bow and midbody for IA, and bow for IB or IC. An alternative arrangement is acceptable only when equivalent_support_status_by_direct_calculation = demonstrated.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The section modulus of a stringer situated within the ice belt shall be calculated using Z = f_6*f_7*p*h*l^2/(m*sigma_y)*10^6 [cm^3] (4.11), and the effective shear area shall be A = sqrt(3)*f_6*f_7*f_8*p*h*l/(2*sigma_y)*10^4 [cm^2] (4.12). Use p from 4.2.2, h from 4.2.1, p*h = 0.15 MN/m when the calculated product is less than 0.15 MN/m, l as stringer span, m from 4.4.3, f_6 = 0.9, f_7 = 1.8, f_8 = 1.2, and sigma_y from 4.3.2.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Set design_line_load_MN_m = max(p_MPa*h_m, 0.15). Compute Z_cm3 = 0.9*1.8*design_line_load_MN_m*l_m^2/(m*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^6 and A_cm2 = sqrt(3)*0.9*1.8*1.2*design_line_load_MN_m*l_m/(2*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^4, with m selected under 4.4.3.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The section modulus of a stringer situated outside the ice belt but supporting ice-strengthened frames shall be calculated using Z = f_9*f_10*p*h*l^2/(m*sigma_y)*(1 - h_s/l_s)*10^6 [cm^3] (4.13), and the effective shear area shall be A = sqrt(3)*f_9*f_10*f_11*p*h*l/(2*sigma_y)*(1 - h_s/l_s)*10^4 [cm^2] (4.14). Use p from 4.2.2, h from 4.2.1, p*h = 0.15 MN/m when the calculated product is less than 0.15 MN/m, l as stringer span, m from 4.4.3, l_s as the distance to the adjacent ice stringer, h_s as the distance to the ice belt, f_9 = 0.80, f_10 = 1.8, f_11 = 1.2, and sigma_y from 4.3.2.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Set design_line_load_MN_m = max(p_MPa*h_m, 0.15) and outside_ice_belt_factor = 1 - h_s_m/l_s_m. Compute Z_cm3 = 0.80*1.8*design_line_load_MN_m*l_m^2/(m*sigma_y_N_mm2)*outside_ice_belt_factor*10^6 and A_cm2 = sqrt(3)*0.80*1.8*1.2*design_line_load_MN_m*l_m/(2*sigma_y_N_mm2)*outside_ice_belt_factor*10^4.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: Narrow deck strips abreast of hatches and serving as ice stringers shall comply with the section modulus and shear area requirements given in 4.5.1 and 4.5.2 respectively. In the case of very long hatches, the classification society may permit the product p* h to be given a value of less than 0.15 but in no case less than 0.10.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Narrow deck strips abreast of hatches and serving as ice stringers shall comply with the section modulus and shear area requirements given in 4.5.1 and 4.5.2 respectively. In the case of very long hatches, the classification society may permit the product p* h to be given a value of less than 0.15 but in no case less than 0.10.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: Regard shall be paid to the deflection of the ship's sides due to ice pressure with respect to very long (more than B/2) hatch openings, when designing weatherdeck hatch covers and their fittings.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Regard shall be paid to the deflection of the ship's sides due to ice pressure with respect to very long (more than B/2) hatch openings, when designing weatherdeck hatch covers and their fittings.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The ice load transferred to a web frame from an ice stringer or from longitudinal framing shall be F = f_12*p*h*S [MN] (4.15). When calculating c_a, use l_a = 2*S. If p*h is less than 0.15 MN/m, use 0.15 MN/m. Use f_12 = 1.8.
requirements.normalized_requirement: The ice load transferred to a web frame from an ice stringer or from longitudinal framing shall be F = f_12*p*h*S [MN] (4.15). When calculating c_a, use l_a = 2*S. If p*h is less than 0.15 MN/m, use 0.15 MN/m. Use f_12 = 1.8.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: If the supported stringer is outside the ice belt, the force F shall be multiplied by (1- hs/ls), where hs and ls shall be as defined in section 4.5.2.
requirements.normalized_requirement: If the supported stringer is outside the ice belt, the force F shall be multiplied by (1- hs/ls), where hs and ls shall be as defined in section 4.5.2.

requirements.source: Ice Class Regulations and the Application Thereof
requirements.source_text: The effective shear area of a web frame shall be calculated using A = sqrt(3)*alpha*f_13*Q/sigma_y*10^4 [cm^2] (4.16), where Q is the maximum calculated shear force under the ice load F from 4.6.1, f_13 = 1.1, alpha is selected from Table 4-8, and sigma_y is the yield stress from 4.3.2.
requirements.normalized_requirement: Compute A_cm2 = sqrt(3)*alpha*1.1*Q_MN/sigma_y_N_mm2*10^4, where Q_MN is the maximum calculated shear force under F and alpha is selected from Table 4-8.
